name: botid.reference-allocator.v1
description: Equal weight among above-average feeds. A feed strictly above the bundle mean gets an equal share of the portfolio; every other feed gets nothing. Outputs are basis points and sum to 10000 whenever at least one feed is above the mean, and to 0 when they are all identical.
note: modelCommitment = keccak256(utf8(name)). Every field here is part of the model's identity: changing the feed count, the output count, the scale or the domain changes the circuit, the verifying key and therefore the agent id. Reputation does not transfer across a change here.
scaleNote: `decimals` is the unit a feed value is quoted in — 100 means cents. `inputScaleBits` is ezkl's `input_scale`: the public input cell holds `value << inputScaleBits`, and it is the third argument to ZkAdapter.setVerifier.
domainNote: `maxAbsValue` is not a style choice, it is where the circuit stops working. halo2 decomposes intermediates in base 2^14 with two limbs, so no intermediate may exceed 2^28. The largest one here is n * maxAbsValue << inputScaleBits = 3 * 300000 * 256 = 2.3e8, just under. Raising either the domain or the scale past that point makes compilation fail outright rather than quietly lose precision — which is the good failure mode, and the reason both numbers live in this file.
